data.title: Iran war drains U.S. blood and treasure
data.description: The war between the U.S. and Iran shows few signs of providing a diplomatic off-ramp, with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio declaring on Wednesday that Tehran "is not serious about talks to end their war" even as the conflict threatens to spread to two of the world's most vital energy chokepoints. Houthi warnings against Saudi shipping sent tankers carrying millions of barrels of crude into costly detours around the Red Sea this week, while Iran's parallel pressure ​on the Strait of Hormuz has pushed oil prices to near six-week highs and gasoline back above $4 a gallon in the U.S. — all as American strikes on Iran continued for an 11th straight ‌night and Tehran targeted U.S.-linked targets in Jordan and Bahrain.
